newsitem.title: USA: N.J. court says homeowners policy covers vandalism.
newsitem.headline: N.J. court says homeowners policy covers vandalism.

text.p: - A homeowner's insurance policy covers the cost of repairing vandalism by the insured's child if not specifically excluded, the state Supreme Court ruled on Tuesday.
The ruling held the Property Casualty Company of MCA should pay Kevin Conway of Ridgewood, N.J., more than $5,500.
The award is Conway's share of liability for damage to a day-care center by his then-15-year-old son and another juvenile in 1991.
The court held unanimously that the insurance policy did not exclude the son's vandalism by covering household "accidents."
"One of the most basic precepts governing judicial construction of insurance policies is that courts construe ambiguities liberally in favor of the insured," Justice Stewart Pollock wrote.

He rejected PCC's argument that granting coverage would lessen the deterrent effect of parental responsibility. Just because the son intended to cause damage is no reason to deny a non-negligent father of protection against vicarious liability, Pollock said.
